Winter ground doesn't forgive a lazy fluid program.
Wet season is here across most of AU and NZ. Ground that ran clean in March starts swelling, sloughing, and grabbing rods.

The crews who get ahead of it adjust their program before the ground forces them to. Not after the bore packs off.

If you haven't reviewed your fluid setup for winter conditions, now is the time. Not next week.
What's the first thing you change in your program when the wet hits?

Every connection is a chance for cuttings to settle.
You stop the pump to make a rod connection. Cuttings start dropping to the bottom of the bore.

Enough settling and the hole packs off around the string. That's how you lose a bore on a job that was running fine.

Carry Flow gels up when the pump stops and holds everything in place. When you start pumping again, it flows clean and carries cuttings out.

Dosage is 1 to 6 kg per 1000L. For tougher conditions, give the team a call and we'll dial it in.
Friday we go deeper on mixing and water compatibility.

The polymer that won't fight you at the hopper.
Most polymers clump if you pour too fast. Carry Flow has a coating that controls how it hydrates, so it mixes clean through the hopper every time.

Works in freshwater, seawater, salt, and brine. The water source changes on site, but Carry Flow doesn't care.

It sits in 6 of our 9 standard fluid programs across sand, gravel, sticky clay, and heavy rock.

Dosage is 1 to 6 kg per 1000L, packed in 15 kg pails. For tougher ground, give the team a call.
Need help dialling in the right program? We're a phone call away.
